comment: A pretty easy trail, however very buggy.  Most of the trail is spent walking through woodland so there's not a lot to see on the way to the falls but once you get there they are quite cool.

Nice easy/moderate trail, most of the elevation near the beginning and end, rest is mostly easy. Well marked, follow the white markers, not very buggy in summer. Waterfalls are both nice.  Around 3/3.5 hrs with a break at devils punchbowl.
We saw THREE snakes
If you wish to include lower punch bowl in your trip, just take a left before starting the right turn for the climb to ridge road.
So so beautiful, prepare for mosquitoes! Recommend going in the morning.
Lovely
Lovely hike. Saw two snakes
Lots of small waterfalls, flowers, birds and a historic stop!
Lots a incline and decline for a challenge, great views of stoney creek and lake ontario and the cities along the north shore.

Very nice trail. Theres markers to follow making it easy to navigate. Lots of waterfalls to look at. Only downside is that it was not fully secluded, some parts you are walking and can see roads and houses. Other than that, very very nice trail.
Nice easy trail, good footing, neither muddy nor icy, not too brutal in terms of hills.  Some sections that would be extremely pretty in fall
Nice trail. Nice views and 2 waterfalls.  Ground frozen on hike to devils punchbowl but on way back as it warmed up got pretty muddy in spots. Never far from city noise but still decent hike
Good easy trail
Felkers falls is beautiful, parking is right next to the main view. Loads of chipmunks!
Only did a bit under a 1/3 of it but really good so far! Can’t wait to go back

Many mushrooms, critters playing on the forest floor, two waterfalls, some up and down, train tracks and an underpass, a barn, and walking along the road for the last stretch to reach devil’s punchbowl.
Took 2.5h. Easy marked Trail. Had steep ups and downs. No bathrooms available
Lots of Wildlife, raccoon on trail! You can’t get down to the waterfall by this trail but still a nice breeze and good views!
Beautiful trail! Went off trail a couple
Doesn’t compare to Dundas Valley. Still beautiful. elevation is most at the halfway point of the trail and towards the end. Wear bug spray !
I’m sad they fenced off the falls.  Hard to see Felker’s!
Very rugged patches and some steep narrow sections. Wear hiking boots.
Great and nice trail, clean.

Decent hike for being in the middle of a city, lots of outside noise and the trails themselves weren't fully maintained. Was more of a moderate hike, good distance to cover the full trail along with some steep hills along the way. Had some good views at the falls themselves but locating the bottom was a bit of a challenge - 7.3/10
Very steep spots, so be prepared for the inclines!
There’s a lot of elevation change, if you walk up the river bed to the base of the punch bowl it’s a lot more fun.
Great hike

Difficult hike but worth it. Free parking
Mostly dry.

This is a
Must DO!! Wet in areas, moderate to hard hike, not well marked.  Sights were beautiful , highly recommended
Great views, well with the hike.

Hiked mid-May on a perfect day -- not hard, but one of the more technically challenging hikes I've found near the GTHA.  Great views and love the waterfalls at both ends!! Decent flow this time of year.
It was amazing
Kim and I went for a sweet hike! She is the bartender and I am the chef.

Wonderful hike with so many beautiful things to look at as you go along. A Waterfall, a river rushing over boulders in some parts, to a whole network of trails to get lost in. Would highly recommend and will definitely hike this again soon.

Nice trail. Steep on the way back but manageable. Only a couple of patches of ice but you will be fine just watch your step. Light traffic, not a lot of people but also not empty. You will see people every 20 mins or so. I was hoping to see Felker’s falls properly but it felt like the view was alright. Otherwise good trail
It’s a very fun trail with ups and downs. Some parts require safety, so hiking boots are definitely recommended.
Great trail. It’s about 10 km start to finish. Only crowded at the falls and Punchbowl.
Has a lot of hills, moderate to hard trail. Views were okay, I expected more based on the pictures.
Good views. Some areas had a lot of road noise
Did Felker Falls to Devils Punch bowl. Lots of hills, rocks in parts of the trail. No washrooms anywhere. Come prepared.
Steep in some parts. Felkers falls only had a dribble of water. Still a great workout.
Great hike
Looootttts of uphill, lots of rocks/roots so not recommended if not in shape or agile
Great condition. Keep in mind the parking at the Punchbowl market is now chained off. Parking at the Conservation center is $8

Lovely 2hr morning hike, surrounded by lots of nature . However, when we got to the devil’s punchbowl (waterfall) , seemed like someone was thirsty and drank all the water. I would still recommend it but if you’re looking forward to the waterfall at the end , it’s currently nonexistent.
Nice morning hike. Muddy and steep in some sections, the rest is all quite dry.

Great trail! Not marked well so be sure to follow the AllTrails map
Amazing view of Hamilton at the end of the hike! 
Lots of wildlife too - would be great for birdwatching!
Nice trail, couldn’t really see the waterfall tho and couldn’t find the way to get down to it. Same with the devils punch bowl. Also had to walk along a busy windy/ blind road for part of it
Pretty waterfalls
Make sure to wear some bug spray. Be concerned about uneven ground and jagged rocks

Mostly dry trail.  The approach to the lookout on the east side of the punchbowl was unmarked and difficult, so difficult that when we got to the top and looked back we noticed a sign stating the trail was closed!  Best to approach the lookout on the trail going up the west side.

Fairly dry trail.
Lots of elevation changes.
Muddy.
We walked the Bruce trail path along the escarpment and down the big cliff path. It's rocky and challenging but the kiddos managed it well. A nice section.
The midpoint of this out and back is actually off trail up the side of the escarpment. When it is muddy like today, it is treacherous, though passable if you can find handholds.
Great train, few muddy spots but nothing too bad. Crazy elevation gains though.
Steep hiking from the lookout scary but found out later there was an easier way…
Trail was good only slightly muddy in spots but nothing you could not easily get around or even go through if needed.
Muddy
Follow the white markings
Muddy

One issue with the route listed is that the last turn going to the look out is off trail, steep, and dangerous. Would highly recommend taking the bruce side trail before the "V" in the route. Much quicker and safer.

it's very nice during winter but expect lots of mud and uneven terrain (rocks). The last leg of the trail goes off the main trail and up the sheer cliff that's actually a blocked off trail in the winter. If the Punchbowl lookout is worth scaling the side of the cliff go ahead but going back down is unsafe and there is no other way to the main trail.
If you are doing this in winter, highly recommend going off trail for a climb from the bottom to the lookout. Had loads of fun doing that! Not sure if it would be possible in summer, though.
Great trail, lots of ups and downs and lots to see.
Excellent trail with 3 waterfalls
Beautiful!
This trail is closed, you should take the bruce side trail. We climbed a mountain to get up here. But it was worth it if you're not afraid.
A little slippery this time of year but a scenic hike
Rocky terrain, Devil's Punch bowl, big cross, mosquitos
It’s so beautiful and peaceful!
Path to the Devil's punch bowl is not marked. Look for the small path up at the fork.

Trail indicated from the Bruce trail up to the lookout is apparently closed as its muddy and washed out in spots and not the safest. You can still use it but it's very steep and slippery. You have to scramble in some spots. Honestly I don't recommend it. Use the Devils Punch bowl side trail if you want it go up to the lookout instead.
Overall this was a pretty intense hike in some spots. There were some steep rocky areas near the Devils Punchbowl but it's worth the trip.
High incline, lots of bugs
Great views, lots of bugs. Trail is well kept but rocky in certain sections. Overall good trail.
definitely bring some bug spray it is a rougher trail with lots of incline was a good time u can also shoot straight up the escarpment if u would like a steeper incline.
Beautiful views on the falls and wonderful hike

Felkers falls was beautiful. Different elevations from Felkers to Punch Bowl. The trail to the Punch Bowl was not clearly marked. There is a gravel hill that will take you to the top. The trail shows you a route with a steep incline that would not be suited for dogs or small children. Made me want to skip the Punch Bowl entirely and I had to find an alternate route to get back. This time of year bug spray is definitely needed. They were out but with the spray I did not get bit.

Great hike for my first ever solo one!! However, I did not bring bug spray because I’m dumb — so I would definitely recommend this. Was a bit muddy because of rain from yesterday, but not too bad. No water flowing into the Devil’s Punchbowl :(  but Felker’s Falls was a gorgeous thing to see!!!

Great trail with variety, will need hiking shoes. The part after Lower punch bowl to the top is extremely steep and unmarked. Once you get to Devil's Punchbowl there is a sign that says trail closed for that part also. And there is a parking lot there as well. I would stop at Lower punch bowl next time. The view from the Devil is underwhelming. Some mosquitos, so bring spray.

Great trail mostly under canopy.  Good markings on the Bruce Trail.  No parking fee on the Felker's Falls parking lot.  
Convenient access.  But because of this, the hum of vehicles is always present, but not too bad.
Plenty of birds and wildflowers.  Typical escarpment features.
Moderate hike.

Nice trail. Peaceful. Moderate difficulty. Mostly easy, but there were some steeper areas. Mostly tree covered. No bugs. Some interesting rock formations. The hike from the base of the devils punch bowl to the top of the observation platform was difficult and the trail was hard to find. The top part was very steep with a narrow path. Be careful. (Consider skipping this part).  On your way back take a 1 km detour to Amica ice cream parlour (Currently open to the public on weekends) This is the old StonyCreek dairy location.
Trail was moderate.  Took my 9 years old nephew with me and he made an 3 hours walk to 2 falls.  Would not bring any young kids to this trail.

Moderate difficulty. Lower punch bowl trail is eroded somewhat. Followed the blue markings up to the lookout points after following the lower unmarked pathways. Bring lots of water and snacks. Not much mud and it was really enjoyable!

The bowl was awesome, make sure you take the side path to get to under the waterfall. If you’ve reached the wooden stairs, you’ve gone too far. The side path is to the right of the waterfall near the wooden stairs.
Great hike! A little rocky and steep in some areas but the Felker’s Falls and Devils Punch Bowl was incredible. 10/10 would recommend!
Did only half way, but the conditions are good.
Lovely lots of snow today

This trail was not my cup of tea. While the trail itself was fairly rugged, it went through a narrow swath of woods with houses and roads within shouting distance the entire way. Lots of inclines. Muddy but all frozen today. Never did find the side path to the Devils punchbowl lookout. The waterfalls were lovely and worth seeing but I won’t be back.
Great trail. Some steep cliffs to be careful with little kids. Otherwise great spot.
Great condition. Very little mud.  Sad to see all the construction garbage strewn over the escapement.
Lovely to have no ice and very little mud

FYI, trail up to the falls is permanently closed (erosion has made it wildly unsafe). You can take the DPB side trail but will have to walk along the road on a narrow shoulder to get to the top it that’s your goal.
Trail is in great condition. Not too muddy. Beautiful views of Felkers Falls and the Devils Punch Bowl.
The last section of the trail upto Devils Punchbwal is a little off from white trail. Need to watch out and not recommend for child
Beautiful hike. Not clear trail markings to get up to devils punch bowl, otherwise amazing
The trail was hard to follow but you can always get to where you’re suppose to go but the devils punch bowl is well worth the hike
Very rocky, but all in all pretty decent.
I completely messed up the last part made it to the platform but pretty sure I took the most difficult route possible.  A great hike brought back memories as a kid growing up in the area
section to devils punchbowl closed and lookout still closed off with police line. the rest of the hike was nice
for the most part is was a good workout, with beautiful scenery. Couldn't get all the way to Devils Punchbowl because the police had the area blocked off...
Some parts of the trail were quite difficult due to the elevation and rocks can get pretty slippery
Trail was nice- at the end when you climb up it is not maintained, realized at top that it is closed so you technically can’t reach the punch bowl at the moment !
Solid trail with some nice views. Shortcut up to devils punch bowl from bruce is a bit tricky though
Not easy to navigate. Definitely wear hiking shoes. Was unable to make it to the punchbowl.
Trail near the punchbowl is not maintain and closed! had to go on a much more difficult route, climbed quite a steep cliffs side instead. NOT a moderate climb at that point.
It is a nice trail but it’s sad to see how dirty the Devil’s punch bowl is
The trail crosses road a few times which isn't ideal, but definitely beginner friendly.
Trail was easy to follow until you get to Devil’s Punch Bowl. Trees down and trail is very narrow at the bottom. Best to take blue side trail to Ridge Road go past bakery to look out point.

Really nice trail! Follow the white markers, easy enough. A bit of up and down elevation, but nothing overly difficult. To get to the bottom of the punchbowl, follow the small path up the creek. Keeping the Lowe falls on your left. Was a bit muddy
Very fun, not muddy anymore
Super muddy. Plenty of water at both falls :)
Super icy, definitely need micro spikes or crampons
Nice out and back but start off trail not open and super icy.
Great trail with some nice elevation changes
Steep with icy sections but the views made it all worthwhile.
Great hike. Turn right and go up the valley to get the best view of the punchbowl from below. There’s currently no established trail going to the lookout point.
Great trail beautiful waterfall.no access to the falls.always wear crampons!
Super icy hike but beautiful. We skipped one section and went above instead. Highly recommend if you are comfortable with icy hikes. Forgot to unpause so trail activity is a bit off.

First trail of 2022. Excellent trail lots of potential during the spring-fall months… gets really icey during winter and can be super hazardous if you’re not careful especially areas where it’s steep. Overall awesome trail wish I could finish it… better safe then sorry will come back during the warmer months!
It was an easy hike but a little icy.
Great to enjoying view and last minute steep hill
Was easy to follow the trail markers but it was extremely muddy. Still great to be able to get so close to the falls.
Great trail, a little too muddy
Lots of ice on the trail￼ today!
Beautiful hike to see these three amazing waterfalls!
Great hike.  All areas are accessible.  the elevations are a good work out.

Nice hike with some challenging elevations but definitely not the most isolated experience - you go through areas that are not far removed from nearby subdivisions. Beautiful fall colours and worth a visit however!
Unbelievable.  Two stunning falls!!  Spectacular challenging trail. Lots of elevation change!!
beautiful!  muddy but amazing
Great little stroll!
Lots of bugs to worry about
Solid trail, hard to find the overgrown path up to the punch bowl but it’s there
For the most part it was a really nice trail, however small segments were overgrown and the segment of trail between Bruce trail and the punch bowl is closed for 2021.
Trail is closed for the final stretch to the devils punch bowl. Can’t see it.
Moderate hike, it felt you in the city as you can hear the cars along the trail
not 100% accurate the one part of the trail is closed but the falls are beautiful. We were a little disappointed with the devil's punchbowl
Really good trail. Good little deviations
Trail was great! Started at Devil's Punchbowl and ended at Felker's Falls. Well marked trail. Only downside is all the litter and graffiti. Definitely needs better on going maintenance.

Single and double white
 markers on trees will keep you on Bruce Trail to Devils Punch Bowl.  Cleared well and moderate challenge with elevation climbs and descends as outlined on map.  Punchbowl dry this time of year.
Great trail but you cannot enter the last leg of this trail to Devils Punchbowl as the trail is closed.
it's alright. wish it was better marked. a bit confusing if its your first time.
I loved this hiking trail! You almost always walk under the shade of the trees. It was definitely easy to complete and also it wasn’t even that crowded on a Sunday comparing to other popular trails.

Beautiful trail with a good amount of challenge. A lot of elevation changes and some narrow trails near steep cliffs. Trails are well maintained. Unfortunately, the last leg to the Devil's Punchbowl was closed off and so we were unable to complete the trail.
Great moderate hike!
Pretty hard for younger kids especially coming down from the top of the falls. Bottom of the falls is great though and needs lots of time to explore
excellent trail. went on a Saturday morning and not too busy! A fairly moderate hike, and you can make it more difficult by climbing down into both falls! would recommend
Terrain is quite rocky and there were some steep parts which we enjoyed.
The views, the intensity and the trees
Dry trail, some rocky portions, some inclines. Overall a good intermediate hike with the punch bowl as a beautiful turn around point.
Great Hike, started from Devils punchbowl to Felkers  fall. At the start it’s steep so have to go down hill bit slippery though. Follow the map signs ain’t that good.

Overall enjoyed the trail. Rocky at certain points and you can see houses and roads and hear city noises but still enjoyable. If you want to get to the base of devils punch bowl you need to go off trail and follow the river/rocks at the end.
Nice mixture of scenery and elevations. I took my dog with me, which was a little scary as there are some steep parts and cliff drops. Really enjoyed the walk!

The hike was great, and challenging. However, toward the end to reach the Devil’s punch bowl it becomes a climb, and gets slightly more dangerous. Also, upon reaching the Devil’s Punch bowl, we were disappointed to see that there was no running water, and it was all dried up.
A beautiful but sticky day ran through both water bottles - Felkers Falls is stunning and this trail section is varied and beautiful.
Great!!
Great
Easy and peaceful!

May 16, 2021.  Decent trail with some up/downhill sections.  Good markings on trail.  Devil’s punch bowl was cool, but that is runoff water. Don’t swim in it.  Last portion of the trail is closed, so you can’t make your way up to the viewpoint.  You can however drive to the viewpoint.
Nice, not overly demanding, however, very rocky.
Great trail. Not too difficult with beautiful highlights at start and finish.

I live in the area and never really explored this trail. It looks like you can have some real fun mountain biking this trail. Escarpment walking trail with nice variations- it’s part of what I call our urban trails ( red hill included ) You will hear traffic noises and see houses below the perimeter. All types of walkers and even spotted a trail runner. Will be a nice add in to my already exciting trail runs.
Great hike. Good elevation! Mud dried up. Highly recommend. Trilliums are about to bloom!
Spectacular views! by the punchbowl you do have to deal with some erosion, so  be careful!
We went to the base of felkers falls.

We took the hike today with the kids. The good part, they could do it, but we did not realize the proximity to urban life.  You could see the houses and roads all the time, hear the grass mover or cars on the busy streets nearby. If this doesn't bother you, then it's a great place to hike. If you are looking for wilderness and quietness, this is not the place.
Fun hike, can be done under 2 hours with a few steep climbs!

Moderately challenging trail. We loved the technicality and elevation in both directions. Great city views in beautiful wooded area. Highly recommend hiking boots. 
Opportunity to hike into punch bowl vs lookout.
Great hike. Almost entirely dry with just a few hard muddy spots. Amazing weather!
Well marked trail, well maintained. Very few muddy areas. Scenic lookout at Devils Punchbowl, but was very windy!!!
nice back and forth trail. some muddy spots. not too much traffic during the weekday. bring lots of water!
Awesome. Little muddy on some places but no major problems.
Pretty muddy and kind of slippery. Once you get past 1.5 kms, it was dry. Trail was steep. I loved it. Not an easy hike
Icy in some spots not to the point where you need cleats, muddy in most - so expect to get a bit dirty. Great trail , well marked.
really icy must have cleats
Awesome! A Little slippery.

Beauty trail with lots of variety and two waterfalls!

Today we were lucky to watch some ice climbing.

We blazed much of the trail after a big snow storm so was hard to track off the start until we got our bearings.
Difficult when icy. Wear ice cleats.

It’s a great trail with a view!  Not suited for little kids as there are sheer drops off the trail but gorgeous views over the city.    I never did the whole trail but definitely plan to go back again.
Ugg
Great hike today. 2hours 25 mins. Follow the white sign posts.
great long trail with lots of height and terrain variation. worth the long walk for the beautiful falls
Well maintained, a bit icy today. Lots of fun

Ice in many places- wear cleats! Otherwise a perfect Covid walk, because  it was sparsely travelled. Poles would be an advantage for the slippery downhill sections. Easily travelled by 2 seniors in 2 hours. Last bit by Devil’s Punchbowl waterfall has a washed out section.
The last part to get to the top of devils falls is closed
Good winter hike with snow. Not hard just a bit up and down. Though not much water at both falls but nice ice and rock formations.

Park at 43 Ackland St.,Stoney Creek, Ontario 
Very rugged and muddy as it just rained the day before but a nice hike especially to see 2 waterfalls.
Devil’s Punchbowl Falls was completely dry on Saturday, Nov. 14th and the trail that leads to the Bruce trail from the punchbowl to take you to Felker’s Falls was closed.
Great leg busting hike with fantastic views of Hamilton and escarpment. Very busy around Devil’s Punchbowl. Very little water on falls but still great hike.
Great Elevation
Beautiful trail!

An intermediate hike with some advanced vertical scrambles at the lunchbowl.  Great views and lots of trail options to lengthen the hike.  Pass by the Stoney Creek Battlefield monument on the route.  Great country bakery neat the bunch bowl at the end.  Beautiful colours for a late Oct hike.

The Devil's Punchbowl waterfall was completely dry at this time of year (late October) despite recent rainfalls. The first part of the trail is nice, and Felker's Falls is impressive, but overall this trail is nothing special.
Amazing trail, hiking along the escarpment. Lots to see, lots of hills, will give you a great workout.
the long way around. not the best route to take.

Sep 6.2020 - Trail is okay, a steep hills and pathway is uneven with many rocks. Shaded for almost the whole path, minimal bugs. Trail markings are decent however, we didn't do any side trails. If not much rain the falls are minimal but still nice to see. They're at the beginning of the trail. Since this is close to residential area you can see homes and hear cars for a stretch of the path. Nice for a hike close to home, just over 8 KMS.
Beautiful long trail and a great hike! I feel their could be more blazes to help guide hikers to stay on the trail.
This trail was great to walk with our 30lbs pup. One disappointment was the view point at Devil’s Punch Bowl was closed (seemed to be for a while, trail had grown over).
Official side trail route leading up to devils Punchbowl is closed but if you turn right after the the stairs on the Bruce trail, there will be a steep ascent that other climbers have been on.
highly recommended dog friendly trail with great views . The section of the trail going up to the devils punchbowl lookout is shut down

This is a beautiful hike! 
We were following the directions in "Hamilton and Area Loops & Lattes" by N. Ross and A. Darrell. To save yourself lost time (indeed we got lost!) there are 3 important items to note:
Be sure to go to the very FAR right of the parking lot on Ackland Street and take the trailhead at the end of the split rail fence where there is no signage. The leftmost trail entrance which splits into 2 trails, mislead us into taking the middle trail instead of the rightmost. 
The blue BTC Devil's Punchbowl Side Trail sign is now almost completely hidden by foliage on young undergrowth trees. This right turn is easily missed when travelling east from Felker's Falls. And yes, we missed it! 
We never located the "shoe tree". It is either fallen, or the shoes have been removed. 

As mentioned by other reviewers, this trail is tricky to follo
More challenging than I thought it would be. We didn't finish half. Trail not always easy to follow or even easy to find.
great tree coverage for those who don't like the hot sun. challenging inclines for beginners

Beautiful hike on the Bruce Trail through the forest after Felker’s Falls. Note that there are some very large drops right beside the trail at Felkers Falls to be very careful of if especially if you have children hiking with you. The Devils Punch Bowl side trail is half on the road but well worth it to the see the bowl and the amazing lookout across Hamilton and Stoney Creek and past to Toronto. There’s a good little stop at the Punch Bowl Market and Bakery along the road to get some fresh treats.  A really nice overall hike. 
This is one of the hikes noted in Hamilton Hikes Loops and lattes books by Nicola Ross and Amy Darrell.
